transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, student health actually sent me here. They said my weight is too low to clear me for the youth workshops I'm supposed to do. I mean, I know the number has kept dropping, but to me, it just feels like what naturally happens when I’m really focused and busy with everything. But they wouldn't sign off on my forms, so that's why I'm here.
Can you tell me how much you currently weigh and how much weight you've lost recently?

I'm actually not exactly sure what my current weight is. When I was at student health, they did weigh me, but I didn't really look at the number. And as for how much I've lost recently... I don't know, I haven't been keeping track of it like that. I just know my clothes fit differently, but I couldn't tell you the exact amount of pounds.
Can you estimate how much weight you think you’ve lost in the past few months, even if it’s just based on how your clothes fit or how you feel?

Um, I really couldn't give you a number. I just... I haven't been keeping track. I mean, my jeans from the start of the semester don't stay up without a belt anymore, and I've had to get a few new things that are a couple of sizes smaller. But as for translating that into actual pounds... I really don't know. It just happened gradually while I was busy with classes, so I honestly couldn't guess.
Can you describe your eating habits lately? Have you been eating regular meals, or have you been intentionally reducing your food intake?

Well, I don't really eat regular meals. I guess I kind of plan my whole day around not eating much. I'll have coffee before my studio classes, and if I'm at the café and people are around, I might have a few bites of something just so they see me eat. But I definitely avoid certain things. Like, I won't touch bread or anything that looks oily. It just feels like eating that kind of stuff would completely undo all the control I've worked for. So, yeah, I guess I have been intentionally reducing it.
Do you feel like your body looks a certain way that you don’t like, even if others might not see it that way?

Yeah, I definitely do. Like, when I look at photos from my recent art showcase, I don't even really see the artwork first. I just immediately zoom in on my arms and my waist. If I look small enough in the picture, it makes me feel like I'm actually serious and put-together. But if I don't... I just feel like I look wrong, no matter what anyone else says.

latest_inference.note: The patient's description of intentional weight loss, preoccupation with body image, and restrictive eating behaviors strongly points to anorexia nervosa (F50.00). Other candidates (E40, E41, E43) are ruled out due to the presence of psychopathology related to body image and eating behaviors rather than单纯的 nutritional deficiency.
